text:
karen_sales: FYI POC with TeraHealth. Streaming sessions keep dropping after ~35-50s when going through their corporate BlueCoast proxy + Azure WAF. After disconnect the client rapidly retries and we see a burst of 429s. Can SEs/Eng swarm?
sam_se: Ack. Which SDKs/versions and are they using mutual TLS or a forward proxy? Any packet captures?
tera_net: Using node-ts-sdk v2.4.x and python-sdk v1.9.x. No mTLS, plain outbound proxy with TLS inspection. We have some raw tcpdump and HAR captures.
dev_infra: Pattern sounds like the proxy terminates long-lived chunked connections. If the client immediately reconnects without honoring Retry-After we hit per-user token rate limits and our rate-limit-bot issues 429. Do you have a sample client log?
tera_net: Short excerpt from Node repro: 
```
[2026-03-26T08:17:03.001Z] stream:start
[2026-03-26T08:17:38.223Z] chunk: data
[2026-03-26T08:18:08.004Z] err: ECONNRESET
[2026-03-26T08:18:08.110Z] retry: attempt=1
[2026-03-26T08:18:08.360Z] http 429 {"error":"rate_limited"}
```
sam_se: Thanks. Immediate recommendations: enable HTTP keep-alive on the client, add heartbeat frames (every 15-20s), and configure SDK retry to use jittered exponential backoff and to respect Retry-After. Also cap concurrent reconnects per session.
dev_infra: Agree. Also check whether BlueCoast rewrites or strips Retry-After and Transfer-Encoding headers — we've seen enterprise middleboxes do that. If Retry-After is lost the client won't back off.
tera_net: BlueCoast does rewrite headers in some cases. Azure WAF also has rules that sometimes remove Transfer-Encoding: chunked.
eng_oncall: Practical immediate mitigations we can provide as SEs:
1) TS: use explicit agent and keepAlive, small socket timeouts, and controlled retry. Example: 
```
const http = require('http');
const agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, keepAliveMsecs: 20000, maxSockets: 6 });
const client = new RedwoodClient({ requestAgent: agent, timeout: 35000, retry: { retries: 5, minTimeout: 500, maxTimeout: 12000, randomize: true } });
// send a no-op heartbeat every 15s while streaming
```
2) Python: requests + urllib3 adapter with respect_for_retry_after enabled: 
```
import requests
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
s = requests.Session()
retry = Retry(total=4, backoff_factor=0.7, respect_retry_after='head')
adapter = HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=8, pool_maxsize=8, max_retries=retry)
s.mount('https://', adapter)
client = RedwoodClient(session=s, respect_retry_after=True)
```
3) If WAF strips chunked encoding, fallback option is buffering small content-length POSTs (1-3 token batches) instead of long chunked stream. Not ideal but stabilizes POC.
4) Use SDK-configured resume/checkpoint tokens so reconnects avoid re-sending full conversation (reduces billable tokens on retries). Note: resume tokens/prefix caching may require Dedicated/Private deployments depending on security posture.
rate-limit-bot: INFO: client-rate-limit: burst=120/min user=tera_net-app1 -> observed 429s at 2026-03-26T08:18Z. Recommend client-slowdown.
tera_net: CFO worried retries will dramatically increase bill. Is there a simple estimate?
sam_se: Retries increase billable tokens only when you resend prompt/history. If client uses full-session resends on reconnect, cost can multiply by tries. With resume tokens or delta updates, retry overhead is tiny. For POC we can test with small resume markers to measure impact.
dev_infra: Longer-term: suggest whitelisting redwood endpoints at BlueCoast or adding an exception for transfer-encoding and Retry-After headers. Also consider increasing per-user burst limits for the POC temporarily (eng_oncall can open a ratelimit override for this customer trial).
tera_net: We can try client changes first. Can you share a minimal repro and a tcpdump filter?
eng_oncall: On it. I'll post two Gists: node+py toggles for keepAlive+retry and a tcpdump command: 
``
sudo tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.ai and tcp and '(port 443)' -w tera_capture.pcap
```
Also include a small Node script that toggles heartbeat vs no-heartbeat so you can repro quickly.
karen_sales: Great. Action items: (1) TeraHealth to try keepAlive + heartbeat + conservative retry (ETA: EOD). (2) Eng to post repro + tcpdump template (ETA: 2 hours). (3) If headers are being rewritten, TeraHealth infra to consider header whitelist or WAF rule change; sales/SE to coordinate escalation for temporary rate-limit bump.
sam_se: I'll join the call if they need live triage.
tera_net: Thanks all, will test and report back tonight.
